strengths: Clear, intuitive, and practical motivation: standard masked diffusion language models make hard binary masking/unmasking decisions at each step, discarding rich predictive distribution information. Soft-masking elegantly addresses this without altering the core transformer architecture.

Minimal parameter overhead: the approach introduces only three learnable scalar parameters (scaling, offset, steepness of the confidence mapping) to govern the continuous feedback in the token embedding space.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental validation: the paper evaluates both pretraining from scratch and continued pretraining on a 169M MDLM, as well as parameter-efficient finetuning (DoRA) on 7B models (Dream-7B, Dream-Coder-7B).
Fair computational accounting: the authors explicitly evaluate both iso-update and iso-compute settings to account for the two forward passes required during self-conditioning training.

Demonstrated compatibility with existing diffusion acceleration methods: soft-masking successfully combines with ReMDM unmasking and Fast-dLLM blockwise caching, showing large gains in high-throughput / low-NFE regimes.
Extensive ablation studies and analysis, including top-k vs. full vocabulary softmax, time-dependent schedules, inference timing overhead breakdowns, and qualitative trajectory visualizations.
weaknesses: Lack of formal probabilistic rigor: unlike some concurrent continuous-discrete hybrid frameworks (e.g., CADD, CANDI) that derive formal marginals and reverse diffusion posteriors, the training procedure here is an empirical two-pass proxy approximation inspired by self-conditioning heuristics.

Diminishing returns at full computation: at full NFE budgets (1/1 ratio), the performance improvements on 7B models become marginal and in some instances slightly negative (e.g., Dream-7B on HumanEval and Math-500), indicating that the primary advantage is concentrated in accelerated/low-step decoding.

Evaluation scope on 7B models is largely restricted to code and math generation; evaluating standard general knowledge and chat capabilities (e.g., MMLU, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval) would provide a more complete picture of general-purpose text generation capabilities.

strengths: Clear motivation and intuitive design: replacing the strict binary decision of retaining or replacing [MASK] tokens with an embedding-space convex combination of the top-k predicted candidates directly tackles the predictive information loss in discrete masked diffusion language models.

Extremely lightweight architecture addition: the confidence-based weighting function relies on negative entropy mapped through a scaled sigmoid, introducing only three scalar trainable parameters without increasing model sequence length or embedding dimensions.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation: tests both pretraining from scratch and pretraining continuation on OpenWebText (169M MDLM), as well as instruction finetuning on 7B models (Dream-7B and Dream-Coder-7B) across multiple coding (HumanEval, MBPP, EvalPlus) and reasoning benchmarks.

Fair computational benchmarking: explicitly accounts for the two-pass training cost by benchmarking under both iso-update and iso-compute settings, proving that soft-masking delivers genuine gains even under strictly matched compute budgets.

Extensive ablations and complementary integration: validates compatibility with existing acceleration frameworks (Fast-dLLM) and advanced unmasking schedules (ReMDM), accompanied by detailed ablations on top-k values, training share, and time-dependent masking.
weaknesses: Performance degradation at full NFE budget on certain tasks: Table 3 indicates that for Dream-7B under the full 1/1 NFE budget, soft-masking slightly degrades accuracy across all coding benchmarks compared to the binary baseline (e.g., -1.7% on HumanEval, -3.0% on HumanEval+). While the gains in low-NFE/high-throughput regimes are compelling, the cause of this high-NFE degradation could be analyzed more deeply.

Heuristic nature of the training approximation: because soft-masking introduces dynamic dependency on the model's intermediate outputs, exact forward marginals become intractable, necessitating a two-pass proxy training objective inspired by self-conditioning rather than a formal generative diffusion derivation.

Training overhead: the two-pass training procedure requires an additional forward pass per optimization step, effectively doubling the forward FLOPs per gradient step during pretraining and finetuning.

strengths: Clear, intuitive motivation: replaces rigid binary masking/unmasking decisions in masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) with continuous feedback via convex combinations of the [MASK] embedding and top-k predicted candidate token embeddings.

Architectural simplicity and minimal parameter overhead: introduces only three scalar trainable parameters governing confidence-based sigmoid weighting, keeping embedding dimensions and model architectures unchanged.
Rigorous experimental design with fair computational accounting: explicitly evaluates both iso-update and iso-compute regimes to account for the two-pass self-conditioning training requirement.

Demonstrated scalability and versatility: evaluated from scratch and via pretraining continuation on small models (169M MDLM on OpenWebText), as well as adapted onto 7B open diffusion models (Dream-7B, Dream-Coder-7B) across standard code and math reasoning benchmarks (HumanEval/+, MBPP/+, GSM8k, MATH-500).

Effective compatibility with orthogonal MDLM acceleration techniques, showing seamless integration and performance improvements alongside advanced remasking schedulers (ReMDM) and KV-caching/blockwise decoding frameworks (Fast-dLLM).
weaknesses: Training cost overhead: The two-pass training methodology inherently requires an extra forward pass per training iteration, substantially increasing training wall-clock time and forward-pass compute.

Mixed or diminished gains at full NFE budgets: As shown in Table 3 (e.g., Dream-7B at NFE 1/1), soft-masking occasionally leads to slight performance regressions compared to binary baselines, indicating that the technique functions primarily as a low-step accelerator rather than improving asymptotic peak generation quality.

Heuristic theoretical formulation: While the paper draws conceptual connections to self-conditioning and uniform diffusion interpolation, soft-masking is primarily an empirical heuristic rather than a formally derived continuous-discrete diffusion process with rigorous ELBO bounds.

Evaluation on 7B models is largely limited to coding and mathematical reasoning; instruction-following and broader open-ended text generation benchmarks (e.g., AlpacaEval, MT-Bench) are not explored at the 7B scale.
